title: Shared dataset-health capability
cold_read: This packet covers "Shared dataset-health capability". 5 of 5 acceptance criteria passed independent verification.
Decide whether to approve the merge request draft. Approval records your decision; it does not merge anything.
context: Give every team one policy-driven way to see which datasets are stale, drifting or unmeasured, and who owns them.

requests.text: Our hotfire review dashboard silently showed three day old engine test data last week. We need to know when the engine_test_runs dataset is stale, with a 60 minute threshold, before every review.
The BOM cost dashboard broke when an upstream column was renamed and nobody noticed for days. We need a check that compares each table schema against its declared contract and reports drift by field.
For the weekly ops review I need an SLA report on the freshness of our NCR tables, grouped by owner team. If a dataset has never been measured it must say unknown, not look fresh.

Three forward deployed engineers each hand-rolled their own dataset freshness checks with different thresholds. We want one shared, reusable capability where thresholds are policy configuration, not code.

overlap.shared_capability: A shared, policy-driven dataset-health capability: freshness against per-dataset thresholds and schema conformance against declared fields, with an SLA report and alerts

distinct_needs.need: Know when a dataset is older than its own threshold, and be alerted before a review
Detect schema drift against a declared contract and name the fields involved
An SLA report grouped by owner team that shows an unmeasured dataset as unknown
One shared capability whose thresholds are policy configuration rather than code

acceptance.description: A dataset older than its own threshold is reported stale and raises an alert
An upstream column rename is reported as schema drift naming the missing and unexpected fields
The SLA report groups datasets by owner team and shows an unmeasured dataset as unknown, never as zero or fresh
Thresholds come from policy configuration; changing only the policy changes the result
Every health record conforms to the pinned HealthRecord contract

remaining_concerns: Drift detection compares declared and observed type names literally
Actual load cadences are not given; thresholds are taken from the requests where stated
Whether an alert should page someone or only appear in a report is not stated
No request says how long drift may persist before it matters
The contract carries no severity ranking; the weekly review may want one
Thresholds in the criteria come from the requests and have not been confirmed by dataset owners
Open question from agt_0mwgq1k8m0ue9f275d1: Should a stale-data alert page someone, or only appear in the report? No request says.
